Subject: Handoff: Dashboard Acceptance Criteria + Runbook Ownership for Kestrel Integration

Hi Emily and Jay,

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, we're starting the observability handoff for the Kestrel integration. The immediate asks from our side are:

- Agree on dashboard acceptance criteria (performance, error slices, SLO panels)
- Confirm tracing hooks and PII masking requirements
- Decide runbook ownership and alert routing for paged vs. non-paged issues

I've attached an initial dashboard spec and a tracing hooks inventory to kick off the discussion (dashboard_spec_v1.pdf, tracing_hooks_list.xlsx). Can you confirm the acceptance criteria below and any compliance constraints by EOD Tuesday so we can lock owners and schedule the delivery sprint?

Proposed owners/timeline:
- Dashboards: Laura Bennett (delivery) — initial draft by 2026-05-27
- Runbook & Alert Routing: Ben Carter (CS Ops) — draft by 2026-05-24
- Security & Masking sign-off: Neha Kapoor — review by 2026-05-26

Proposed next step: 60-min coordination call Tuesday 2026-05-19 10:00 AM PT. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Thanks,

Sergio Álvarez
Commercial Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: dashboard_spec_v1.pdf, tracing_hooks_list.xlsx)

From: Emily Richards <emily.richards@kestrelhealth.com>

Date: 2026-05-19T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Dashboard Acceptance Criteria + Runbook Ownership for Kestrel Integration

Hi Sergio,

Appreciate the clear list — this matches what we need. A few clarifications and acceptance bullets from Kestrel: 

- Dashboards must show 99th/95th/median latency and error rate broken down by service and dataset
- Include a repro-rate panel (fraction of requests that trigger a reproducible failure)
- Tracing: we need span-level metadata but must redact any user-identifiable fields (PII masking required)
- Alerts: only P2/P1 (rate spikes, model errors causing service degradation) should page on-call; noisy low-priority alerts should route to a ticketing queue

We also need the runbook template to include a section for customer impact classification and a checklist for rollback steps. If you can attach your runbook template, we'll review and mark owners on our side.

Confirming the 10:00 AM PT call on 2026-05-19 — that works for us.

Thanks,

Emily Richards
Implementation Lead
Kestrel Health

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT, Emily Richards <emily.richards@kestrelhealth.com> wrote:

>

I've sketched an initial implementation checklist and owners below — attaching a runbook template (runbook_draft.md) and the first dashboard wire PDF.

Implementation checklist (high level):
1) Wire dashboards: panels for latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, repro-rate, and top error buckets — owner: Laura — draft 2026-05-27
2) Instrumentation: confirm and add tracing hooks for the three critical flows (ingest, transform, serve) — owner: Ben — complete by 2026-05-24
3) PII masking: apply field-level redaction in spans per Neha's guidance — owner: Neha — sign-off by 2026-05-26
4) Alert routing: map alerts to on-call vs ticketing, create alert suppression rules for noisy signals — owner: Ben — draft 2026-05-24
5) Runbook: include impact classification, rollback checklist, communication steps, runbook ownership and contact info — owner: Ben — draft 2026-05-24
6) Dry run: simulated incident run-through on 2026-05-29 with Kestrel ops — all owners present

Notes:
- I'll add explicit panel queries for service/dataset breakdowns and share the dashboard JSON for review.
- Please review the runbook structure in the attachment and add any Kestrel-specific fields.

Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
(attachment: runbook_draft.md)
